A1.justification: Both PDFs describe iiANET and iiABlock. All supplied pages, including figures, tables, equations and end matter, support comparison. Neither version contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original iiANET classification, COCO detection and instance-segmentation results, Grad-CAM visualizations, and component, channel-ratio, attention-head and register ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original iiANET experimental outcomes, including classification and COCO results and the ablations in Tables 4–6.

M1.justification: V1 defines iiABlock fusion through concatenation in Section 3.2 and Figure 3. V2 adds channel shuffling after concatenation in Section 3.1.4, Equation 8 and Figure 2. The convolutional and attention branches and stage counts are otherwise retained; the inverted-bottleneck, atrous-convolution and r-MHSA terminology largely renames existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate classification on AID, Oxford-III, RLD and ImageNet-1K, and detection and instance segmentation on COCO-2017. V2's references to semantic segmentation do not introduce corresponding evaluation data or results.

E2.justification: The corresponding classification, detection, instance-segmentation and qualitative comparisons retain their comparator membership. CrossViT and DFANet are newly cited but not evaluated. YOLOv8 replaces the detector label for iiANET itself, rather than adding a baseline.

E3.justification: The COCO detection table changes iiANET's detector from Faster R-CNN in v1 to YOLOv8 in v2. This is a reported setting revision, but v2's caption and surrounding prose still specify Faster R-CNN, leaving the actual detector unresolved. Other reported training budgets, input sizes, metrics and evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Tables 4–6 retain the same component-removal, channel-ratio, attention-head and register-count ablations. Figures 1, 4 and 6 retain the same qualitative examples. No new analysis isolates the added channel-shuffling operation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical scores and qualitative examples are unchanged. The classification table retains iiANET top-1 accuracies of 79.34% on ImageNet-1K, 80.57% on AID, 74.04% on Oxford-III and 94.79% on RLD. COCO detection values remain 62.6 and 63.0 despite the changed detector attribution; no performance gain is established.

T1.justification: The formal block-output definition is extended to a shuffled representation in v2 Equation 8, whereas v1 ends at concatenation. V2 also writes out the atrous-convolution operation in Equation 2. The existing attention/register equations and channel-splitting algebra are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V2 reframes the abstract and contributions around iiABlock and interaction between fused features, and removes v1's explicit claim to be the first hybrid model integrating registers. The principal claims about efficient long-range dependency modeling, competitive performance and backbone applicability remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explicit limitation that iiANET may be less effective on localized-object datasets such as ImageNet-1K and tasks with little long-range context. It also adds interpretations of atrous convolution as bridging local and global representations and channel shuffling as strengthening interaction between branches.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository pointer in the abstract and explicit stage-resolution documentation. Hardware and training hyperparameters are retained, and the 2/3/5/2 stage counts were already shown in v1 Figure 2. The redrawn component diagram omits v1's explicit expansion-factor label and separate stem/max-pooling panel.

R1.justification: V2 retains the original 50 references and adds CrossViT and DFANet as references 51–52. Section 3.1.4 positions its fusion against their cross-attention and feature-aggregation approaches. The first-hybrid-with-registers novelty claim is also removed, while the broader related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution passages are rewritten, and the method exposition is substantially reorganized around iiABlock. New subsections separate local details, global details, feature recalibration and fusion, followed by the relocated network overview. Terminology changes and added limitations, funding and dataset-usage declarations further revise the document structure.

P2.justification: The architecture figures exchange numbering and position. The component diagram is redrawn with a shuffle operation, revised labels and rearranged panels; the network overview gains spatial-resolution annotations. Existing Grad-CAM displays and result-table structures are retained, with resizing and page reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 improves method exposition, adds a code-access pointer and acknowledges an applicability limitation. However, it introduces channel shuffling without explaining its relationship to the unchanged experimental results, and creates a direct YOLOv8 versus Faster R-CNN inconsistency in the COCO evaluation. These gains in explanation coexist with increased ambiguity about the evaluated system, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
